guidelines.detail: documentation rule FLOW-05 not applied (The validator reports that a `<default>` child is unexpected where an outgoing flow is expected, supporting an XML-encoding error. Documented guideline FLOW-05 already specifies the correct representation, so this is not a new modeling rule.)

same as LRN-008 (The description identifies submission as an action that starts the process. The generated start event has no reference counterpart, while the reference submission activity has no generated counterpart, indicating that the start event was used in place of the action. This is the situation already covered by LRN-008.)

refines FID-01 (The description explicitly mentions IT support after rollout, but the generated end-event label absorbs that outcome and the reference has a separate support task with no generated counterpart. This refines the general instruction to model every distinct activity by clarifying how to model post-completion support. No extra-element record was provided to check for an alternative generated counterpa)

same as LRN-005 (The records show multiple reference sequence flows absent from the generated model. The description supports an ordered process with a conditional approval outcome, and LRN-005 already covers preserving order and branch-and-join structure.)

same as LRN-024 (The description explicitly includes compatibility checks and a controlled testing environment, while the matched reference labels omit those distinguishing details. This is already captured by learned guideline LRN-024.)

refines FID-01 (The description states that the request is assessed, including a compatibility check, while the records identify the corresponding assessment activity as missing. This refines FID-01 by clarifying how to model a stated assessment. No generated-element-without-counterpart record was provided to indicate that the work was modeled using another element.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: Reference a default flow with the source activity or gateway default attribute and give the default flow no conditionExpression.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies a default route among the outgoing paths of a decision

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process begins when a participant performs an action: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the described action as an activity after that event; do not use the start event alone to represent the action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description indicates that ongoing support is available after the main work is completed: Model the support as an activity in the process flow rather than mentioning it only in an end-event label.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description indicates that ongoing support is available after the main work is completed

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an order among process stages, describes branches that converge, or says that multiple required activities must finish before a later stage or process completion: Model the sequence flows that connect the corresponding elements, preserving the stated order and branch-and-join structure. Use gateway types that match whether the description specifies a choice or requires all branches to complete.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an order among process stages, specifies decision outcomes, or says that multiple required activities must converge before later work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity together with a purpose, object, or scope that distinguishes what is being done: Label the corresponding BPMN task with its core action and enough of those stated details to preserve the activity’s meaning; do not add unsupported details or omit details that distinguish it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity with a scope, criterion, or execution context that distinguishes what is being done

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description explicitly states a distinct assessment, review, or check as part of the process: Model that work as a separate BPMN activity and connect it according to the described dependencies; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description explicitly states a distinct assessment, review, or check as part of the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states a conditional branch but does not state the outcome when the condition is not met: Label any corresponding end event generically; do not infer an unstated outcome from the condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a conditional branch but does not state the outcome when the condition is not met
